speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an 8-year-old having trouble sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened; can you tell me exactly what happens during these scary moments and if anyone else is in the room with you?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. The patient's history of waking up frightened with intact recall and ability to be consoled, without confusion, is consistent with nightmares rather than sleep terrors. These episodes occur 1-2 times per week for 2 months, causing daytime fatigue.
